'''Jonathan A. Jones''' (born 1967) is a professor in [[atomic physics|atomic]] and [[laser physics]] at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref name="oxphysics">{{cite web |title=Jonathan Jones |url=https://www2.physics.ox.ac.uk/contacts/people/jjones |website=www2.physics.ox.ac.uk |publisher=University of Oxford, Department of Physics |access-date=29 August 2018 |language=en}}</ref> and a [[fellow]] and tutor in physics at [[Brasenose College, Oxford]].<ref name="BNC">{{cite web | url = http://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/323/about-brasenose-31/academic-staff-150/professor-jonathan-jones-457.html | title = Brasenose College: Professor Jonathan Jones | access-date = 24 August 2013 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130922044742/http://www.bnc.ox.ac.uk/323/about-brasenose-31/academic-staff-150/professor-jonathan-jones-457.html | archive-date = 22 September 2013 }}</ref>

==Education==
Jones studied at [[Corpus Christi College, Oxford]], from 1985 to 1989 and [[St John's College, Oxford]], from 1989 to 1992. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1992 for research on Nuclear magnetic resonance data processing methods supervised by [[Peter Hore (chemist)|Peter Hore]].<ref name=dphil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|title=Nuclear magnetic resonance data processing methods|first= Jonathan A.|last=Jones|date=1992|url=https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:7df97c9a-4e65-4c10-83eb-dfaccfdccefe|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.314864}}|oclc= 863543024|website=ora.ox.ac.uk}} {{free access}}</ref>

==Research and career==
Although trained in [[chemistry]], he is active in [[physics]], especially for his work on [[Nuclear magnetic resonance|NMR]] [[quantum computation]] for which he was awarded the 2000 [[Marlow Award|Marlow Medal]] of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name="Marlow">{{cite web | url = https://www.rsc.org/standards-and-recognition/prizes/research-and-innovation-prizes/faraday-early-career-prize-marlow-prize | title = Faraday early career prize: Marlow Prize | access-date = 18 October 2026 | publisher = [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]}}</ref> His main research interest is in [[quantum computation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://users.ox.ac.uk/~jajones/|title=Jonathan Jones personal home page|website=users.ox.ac.uk}}</ref>

==Freedom of information activism==
In 2009, Jones joined in making [[Freedom of Information requests to the Climatic Research Unit]] following a complaint by blogger [[Steve McIntyre]] that the [[Climatic Research Unit]] of the [[University of East Anglia]] (UEA) had refused to release raw weather station data. Meteorological organisations had allowed the university to use this data on the understanding that it would be kept private, largely due to its commercial value. Jones made a [[Freedom of information in the United Kingdom|Freedom of Information]] request for raw data which the university had shared with another researcher, but refused to provide to McIntyre. The university worked with the [[Met Office]] to get meteorological organisations to waive confidentiality on raw instrumental data, most failed to respond and two refused. In 2011 the [[Information Commissioner's Office]] decided that the university had to make the data public, regardless of the wishes of its owners. Jones said to [[BBC News]] that it was a matter of principle, "This dataset wasn't particularly interesting, but we thought the data in general should be available, and we thought people shouldn't have to make FoI requests for it."<ref name="beeb 27 July 2011">{{Cite web  | last = Black | first = Richard | title = Climate unit releases virtually all remaining data | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-14315747 |publisher=[[BBC News]]|website=bbc.co.uk  | date = 27 July 2011 | access-date =30 August 2015 }}</ref> The decision was described as a "landmark ruling" and a "victory for critics of the UEA" by [[Fred Pearce]] of ''[[The Guardian]]''. Jones said "My sole aim [in pursuing the case] is to help restore climate science to something more closely resembling scientific norms".<ref name=Pearce>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2011/jul/01/climate-data-uea|first=Fred|last= Pearce|date=1 July 2011|website=[[The Guardian]]|title=Oxford academic wins right to read UEA climate data}}</ref>
